sections.h2: What should a Sunrise homeowner know before selling quickly?
sections.html:
Sunrise sellers have three routes: list with an agent, sell on their own, or take a cash offer, and the city's permit rules and Broward County's records shape each one. Sunrise is a planned city on the western edge of Broward County, so many homes were built in the decades when it grew from a golf village into a city of more than 98,000 residents, according to the city.

Fast sales hinge on documents. Gather the deed, any homeowners association papers, permit records and a recent tax bill, and you can answer a buyer's questions in a day instead of a week.

sections.h2: How did Sunrise grow from a golf village to a city?
sections.html:
The City of Sunrise says it was incorporated in 1961 by a developer who bought 2,650 acres on what was then the remote western edge of Broward County. It began as Sunrise Golf Village with about 350 residents, and a referendum changed the name to the City of Sunrise in 1971 when the population reached 15,000.

The city's history page describes an estimated 50,000 residents by October 1984, the 612-acre Sawgrass International Corporate Park added in 1987, Sawgrass Mills mall opening in 1990, and the arena opening in 1998. Through annexation the city now covers more than 18 square miles, reaching the Everglades and extending south of I-595 and State Road 84.

It sits about six miles west of Fort Lauderdale and adjoins Weston, Davie, Tamarac, Lauderhill and Plantation.

sections.h2: What does Sunrise offer buyers nearby?
sections.html:
The city says its neighborhoods range from private luxury communities to affordable options that include well-kept rental properties, and it counts 20 parks, a golf course, a tennis club, municipal pools, a senior center and a civic center with a 300-seat theater. It lists eleven public schools, two post offices and a public library.

Highway access is a listing point: the city says it is bordered by the Sawgrass Expressway, I-75 and I-595 and lies near the Florida Turnpike and I-95, with access to three airports and three seaports. Sawgrass Mills and the Sunrise Business and Entertainment District, home to the Florida Panthers' arena, draw visitors from across the region.

Since 2014 the city says it has completed or begun about $356 million in capital improvements, including a 95,000-square-foot City Hall that opened in 2023, and it has not raised its millage rate since 2009. Mention these when a buyer asks what the area offers.

Sunrise runs a two-level process: work that changes a building's footprint or exterior goes through Broward County and the city's Community Development Department, while smaller jobs go straight to the Building Division. The city says re-roofing, interior renovation, fencing, interior plumbing or electrical repairs and AC changeouts do not need Planning and Development review.

City of Sunrise permit steps, as listed on the city permitting page
StepWhat happens
1. Choose where to fileDemolition, additions, alterations and new construction need Broward County approval first, then city review
2. File the applicationThe city issues a Control Number used for the whole approval
3. Correct plansApplicant is notified of corrections; Wednesday mornings are Professional Day
4. Receive the permitIssued after structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and fire approvals; fees due at submittal

The Building Division's number is (954) 572-2354, and the city accepts applications electronically. If a previous owner added a room or screen enclosure, ask the division whether it was permitted and finaled.

sections.h2: Which Sunrise permit issues slow a sale?
sections.html:
Unfinished permits and unpermitted additions cause the most trouble, because they surface during a buyer's title or inspection review.

  • Additions or garage conversions that changed the exterior, which need both county and city sign-off.
  • Roof, AC and plumbing work done by a contractor without a final inspection.
  • Fences and other work done without any permit.

If you find a gap, you have two options: close it before listing, or disclose it and let the price reflect it. A cash buyer will usually accept either, but get the terms in writing. Do not assume a seller's report is enough, since lenders and title companies pull their own records.

sections.h2: How do Broward County property taxes affect a Sunrise sale?
sections.html:
Broward's property appraiser values the home each January 1 and the tax collector mails bills in November, so a closing in the second half of the year involves prorating the full-year bill. A sale also ends the seller's Save Our Homes cap, and the buyer's assessment moves to just value on the next January 1.

Florida allows a homestead exemption of up to $50,000 when the owner files by March 1 and has made the home the permanent residence by January 1. Owners 65 or older may qualify for an extra local exemption if the city or county has enacted one and income limits are met, so ask the Broward County property appraiser which apply to your address.

Paying in November earns Florida's printed 4 percent discount, dropping by one point each month through February.

sections.h2: What do stamp tax and recording cost on a Sunrise deed?
sections.html:
Broward deeds pay Florida's standard documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration; the Department of Revenue lists Miami-Dade as the only county with a different structure. The clerk collects it at recording and all parties to the document are liable.

Per-page clerk fees come from section 28.24: $5.00 for page one, $4.00 after, and added per-page charges. Title insurance and lien payoffs come on top.

Ask any buyer for a written cost split before signing, covering who pays stamp tax, title and recording, and whether the offer depends on an inspection.

sections.h2: What is the Upside-Down House story in Sunrise?
sections.html:
The city's early marketing hook was a model home built entirely upside down, with furniture, fixtures, landscaping and even a convertible in the carport turned over. The city says it drew 12,000 visitors in its first four days, was featured in Life Magazine and was demolished in 1975 after more than one million visitors.

It is a fun piece of local history and a reminder that Sunrise grew by marketing home lots to buyers. When you sell, the same principle applies: show what the house offers clearly, with records ready and repairs explained.

sections.h2: How should a Sunrise seller compare a listing with a cash offer?
sections.html:
Compare them on timeline, certainty and net proceeds. A listing exposes the house to the widest group of buyers but adds showings, inspection negotiations and financing risk. A cash offer trades some price for a faster, more predictable close.

  • Ask each buyer for the closing date in writing.
  • Ask what happens if their inspection finds permit gaps.
  • Confirm who orders and pays for the title search.
  • Ask whether proof of funds is available on request.

A Sunrise home with a finished permit file, a clear tax picture and a deed ready to record is easy to price either way. If the house carries a mortgage, request a payoff letter first so you know the minimum you can accept.

faqs.q: Does Sunrise have its own building division?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Sunrise Building Division handles permits at (954) 572-2354. Work that changes a building's exterior or footprint also goes through Community Development, and larger jobs need Broward County approval first.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace my roof in Sunrise?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. The city lists re-roofing among work submitted directly to the Building Division. Confirm with the division before work begins and keep the final inspection record.

faqs.q: Is the documentary stamp rate different in Broward County?
faqs.a: No. Broward uses the standard 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Only Miami-Dade has a different structure under the Department of Revenue's published rates.

faqs.q: Will my homestead exemption stay with the house?
faqs.a: No. The buyer must apply for their own exemption by March 1, and the assessment resets to just value after the sale because a sale is a change of ownership.
